newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-LAPASSET VOWS TO REFORM FRENCH RUGBY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LAPASSET VOWS TO REFORM FRENCH RUGBY.

text.p: Bernard Lapasset, re-elected unopposed as president of the French Rugby Federation (FFR) on Saturday, pledged himself to reforms needed to bring France in line with the new professionalism in rugby union.
Lapasset, who will head the FFR for another four years, said: "We are going to be able to get down to some serious work in thinking about the indispensable reforms for the rugby of tomorrow."
France, like their fellow Europeans in Britain, are lagging behind the southern hemisphere powers in international rugby.
They were beaten in both tests at home during South Africa's tour of France that ended last weekend.

They will be looking to rebuild quickly for the Five Nations tournament next year as a vital step on the road to challenging the supremacy of South Africa, New Zealand and Australia in the 1999 World Cup.
Former FFR vice-president Marcel Martin withdrew his candidacy at the head of the "Rugby for all" opposition grouping after several members defected on Friday.
